newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas steady to lower in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas steady to lower in light trade.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were little changed Friday in light trade, with a slight downward move on NYMEX pressuring eastern prices ahead of the weekend, market sources said.
Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was pegged one cent lower at C$1.45-1.47 per gigajoule.
Sources said most traders were not involved in forward business.
At Sumas, Wash., prices were still quoted at $1.17-1.20 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
Similarly at Station 2, prices were talked at C$1.55 per GJ.
A 20-day maintenance outage is scheduled to begin Sunday at Westcoast Energy's 350 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) Pine River gas plant in northeastern British Columbia.

The plant was expected to process about 175-180 mmcfd of gas for most of the period. On Aug 27 and 28, the flow rate was scheduled to drop to zero but then climb back up to about half-capacity until the work is completed on Sept 7.
In the East, Niagara prices drifted a few cents lower to the mid-$2.60s as NYMEX September futures slipped to a low of $2.395 today, down 3.3 cents from Thursday's settlement.

Separately, Canadian Gas Association reported earlier today that total gas stocks as of last week were at 295.82 bcf, or 59.8 percent full, compared with 63.6 percent a year ago. In the East, stocks rose to 130.47 bcf, or 56.1 percent, while western stocks were at 165.35 bcf, or 60 percent full.
